sources.label: Microsoft: Outlook calendar API and supported mailbox data
Microsoft: user and administrator consent
Apple: multiple calendars and read-only subscriptions

guides.assessment: Mailbox hosting, device-versus-direct connection, Premium versus organisational approval, provider permission and mirror-storage limits are substantive and bounded. One incomplete hide-first diagnostic step needs the established selection side-effect and restoration qualification.
guides.confidence: High semantic comparison confidence; moderate factual confidence bounded to recorded source evidence, not runtime.

proposals.before: Before adding another connection, inspect where the existing work calendar appears. If you later see two versions of a meeting, identify their calendar sources and hide one temporarily. Avoid using account removal or event deletion to diagnose which connection produced them.
proposals.after: Before adding another connection, inspect where the existing work calendar appears. If you later see two versions of a meeting, identify their calendar sources and hide one temporarily. Avoid using account removal or event deletion to diagnose which connection produced them. In Cloud Calendars, record the original selection and restore it after comparing. Selection can also affect widgets and notification scheduling; do not assume it is only a display preference.
proposals.rationale: Existing instruction actively asks the reader to hide a source. Recorded selection consumers include widgets/notification scheduling, so leaving out restoration and downstream effect can disrupt the schedule beyond the diagnostic view. This is a bounded task-completeness defect, not a falsehood in Microsoft tier/compatibility prose.
proposals.evidence: research/batch26-duplicates/product-evidence.json /evidence CalendarViewModel selection consumers and /distinctions Calendar selection
proposals.limits: No universal provider pause/resume claim; no Microsoft synchronization timing or semantics inferred.
